title: Protocol Buffers wire format (field tag)
summary: A protobuf-encoded message is a sequence of fields, each encoded as (field_number << 3) | wire_type followed by the value. Wire types: 0 varint, 1 64-bit, 2 length-delimited, 3 start group (deprecated), 4 end group (deprecated), 5 32-bit.
source_version: Wikipedia List of file signatures, retrieved 2026-05-29

notes: Wire type 0 (varint): zigzag-encoded signed ints, bools, enums.
Wire type 2 (length-delimited): strings, bytes, embedded messages, packed repeated fields.
Field tag = (field_number << 3) | wire_type; field numbers 1-15 use 1 byte, 16+ use 2 bytes.
No self-describing schema: the .proto definition is needed to decode.
